title: Describe the main components of the CPU. · earlier version

slides.name: 1 · Describe the main components of the CPU.

params.text: Describe the main components of the CPU.
Computer Science (GCSE) · Command word 2: Describe · What are its characteristics?

slides.notes:
Aim: describe the CPU’s main components, each with its specific role, and know what that answer has to contain.
From the Nodes stage: https://the-teaching-model.vercel.app/framework/gcse-cs/2

slides.name: 2 · Do Now: answer in your book

params.text: Do Now: answer in your book

Task (3 min): answer the three questions on your own. No notes.
1. What does CPU stand for?
2. In one sentence: what does the CPU do?
3. What is hardware?

slides.notes: 3 min, on entry. Retrieval of earlier learning only: the Define lesson (command word 1) and earlier work on hardware. If the class has not met these, swap in three questions from their last lesson.

feedback.prompt: Your three answers, one per send.

slides.name: 3 · Do Now: answers

params.data:
Question	Answer
1. What does CPU stand for?	Central Processing Unit
2. What does the CPU do?	It executes (carries out) program instructions.
3. What is hardware?	The physical parts of a computer system.

slides.notes: 1 min. Students tick or correct in a different colour. Answer 3 is the AQA mark scheme’s own (8525/2, June 2023, Q8.1: physical components of a computer system).

slides.name: 4 · Today

params.text: I can describe the main components of the CPU, each with its specific role.

I name each part exactly.
I say what each part does, or what it holds.
I avoid labels like “the brain” and vague words like “stores data”.

slides.notes: 1 min. Read the three success criteria aloud. Students check their own answers against them at the end.

slides.name: 5 · The question we will answer

params.text: Describe the main components of the CPU.
Your answer should give: A list of components, each with its specific role

“Describe” means: say what each part is like, or what it does.
For this question: name each part, then give its job.

slides.notes: 1 min. Point at the command word, then at “its specific role”: that phrase is the whole job.

slides.name: 6 · Have a go first

params.text:
Task (3 min): answer the question in your book. Name each part you know and say what it does.
It is fine not to know yet: this shows where you are starting.
Keep it: you will compare it with your answer at the end.

slides.notes: 3 min. Collect, do not correct. Then ask of two answers: “What does that mean it actually does?” A student who can then say it has the knowledge and needs expression; one who cannot needs the content.

feedback.prompt: Describe the main components of the CPU.

slides.name: 7 · Section · The parts of the CPU
slides.notes: The diagram is the Nodes Plan view (the Visual tab).

slides.name: 8 · Inside the CPU

params.text:
This is a plan of a CPU, seen from above.
You need six parts for this answer:
control unit, ALU, registers, the PC, cache and clock.
Main memory and the buses sit outside the CPU.

slides.notes: 1 min. Let the class look. Point to each part as you name it. Main memory and the buses come into the new task at the end.

slides.name: 9 · 1. Control unit

params.text:
In plain words: It works out what each instruction means, then tells the other parts what to do, and when. It DOES something.
Write this in your book: Control unit: decodes instructions and sends control signals that coordinate the other parts.

slides.notes: 1 min. The plain words first, then the exam wording, which stays bright: students copy it into their book.

slides.name: 10 · 2. ALU (arithmetic logic unit)

params.text:
In plain words: It does the maths (add, subtract) and the logic (compare two values, AND, OR). It DOES something.
Write this in your book: ALU: performs arithmetic and logical operations.

slides.notes: 1 min. The plain words first, then the exam wording, which stays bright: students copy it into their book.

slides.name: 11 · 3. Registers

params.text:
In plain words: Tiny, very fast stores inside the CPU. Each one holds one thing the CPU is using right now. They HOLD something.
Write this in your book: Registers: tiny, fast stores inside the CPU.

slides.notes: 1 min. The plain words first, then the exam wording, which stays bright: students copy it into their book.

slides.name: 12 · 4. PC (program counter)

params.text:
In plain words: An address is a location in memory. The PC holds the location of the next instruction. It HOLDS something.
Write this in your book: PC: holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched.

slides.notes: 1 min. The plain words first, then the exam wording, which stays bright: students copy it into their book.

slides.name: 13 · 5. Cache

params.text:
In plain words: Small, fast memory that keeps what the CPU uses often, so it does not wait for main memory. It HOLDS something.
Write this in your book: Cache: fast memory close to the processor, for frequently used data and instructions.

slides.notes: 1 min. The plain words first, then the exam wording, which stays bright: students copy it into their book.

slides.name: 14 · 6. Clock

params.text:
In plain words: It sends a steady pulse, a timing signal, that keeps every part working in step. It DOES something.
Write this in your book: Clock: provides timing signals that keep the CPU's operations in step.

slides.notes: 1 min. The plain words first, then the exam wording, which stays bright: students copy it into their book.

slides.name: 15 · Does it DO something, or HOLD something?

params.text: Does it DO something, or HOLD something?
Some parts do work. Registers only hold.

Do work: the control unit, the ALU, the clock.
Hold one thing: registers (PC, MAR, MDR, CIR, ACC) and cache.
Why it matters: examiners mark “the MAR fetches data” wrong. A register holds; it never fetches.

slides.notes: 2 min. Mixed up in 15 examiner findings across AQA, Cambridge, OCR, Pearson: cpu parts and what they hold or do.

slides.name: 16 · Quick check: do or hold?

params.text:
Task (1 min): decide for each part: does it DO something or HOLD something? Vote on your phone, or hands up.
The MAR (memory address register)

slides.notes: 1 min. Then the answer slide.

feedback.prompt: The MAR: does it do something or hold something?

params.text:
It holds an address: where in memory the CPU is reading from or writing to.
It does not fetch. The control unit directs the fetching.

slides.name: 18 · Section · How to write the answer
slides.notes: Complete what this question requires: no more reasoning than it asks for, and no less precision.

slides.name: 19 · The rule for this answer

params.text: Name the part → give its specific job

Do this for every part.
One part, one job, one line.
No more reasoning than the question asks for, and no less precision.

slides.notes:
1 min. This is the join Nodes gives for “describe components”. It is mostly recall: a pairing, not a chain of reasons. So the fix is precision, not more “because”.
From the Nodes stage: https://the-teaching-model.vercel.app/framework/gcse-cs/2

slides.name: 20 · Answers that lose the mark

params.data:
Mistake	Example	Why it loses the mark
A label	“The CPU is the brain of the computer”	It does not say what it does.
An action for a holder	“The MAR fetches data”	Registers hold. They do not fetch.
The wrong name	“Main memory” when the question means RAM	Use the exact term the question needs.

slides.notes:
1 min. Each is a refusal the mark schemes record. A mark scheme’s own warning to markers: “Careful that the purpose is not an action such as fetches, takes, retrieves.” (OCR GCSE J277/01, June 2024, Q6(b)).

slides.name: 21 · Watch: the answer, one part at a time

params.text: Watch: the answer, one part at a time

Control unit: decodes instructions and sends control signals that coordinate the other parts
ALU: performs arithmetic and logical operations
Registers: tiny, fast stores inside the CPU
PC: the PC holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched
Cache: fast memory close to the processor, for frequently used data and instructions
Clock: provides timing signals that keep the CPU's operations in step

slides.notes: 3 min, one line per click. THINK ALOUD for each: "Which part? What exactly does it do or hold? Would these words fit any other part? Then they are not precise enough."

slides.name: 22 · Section · Spot the mistakes
slides.notes: Three made-up answers, written for Nodes (its Students A, B and C).

slides.name: 23 · Three answers to the same question

params.text: Three answers to the same question

A weak answer: misses the point.
A stable answer: some parts right, some not exact.
An excellent answer: every part with its exact job.
They are made up, so we can practise marking them.

slides.notes: 30 s. In Nodes these are Students A (weak), B (stable) and C (excellent): the same three on the Question tab.

slides.name: 24 · The CPU has a hard drive and RAM.

params.text: The CPU has a hard drive and RAM.
— The weak answer. Task (1 min): with your partner, say what is wrong with it.

slides.notes:
1 min. Take two answers, then the next slide.
Possible explanation: Names storage and memory, not the CPU’s own components. Probe: “Take one component. What does it do while a program runs?” If that is not enough: “The PC holds an address. The address of what?” Then withdraw the hint and ask for the full description of each component. Teaching response, if the probe confirms it: secure the term and its exact meaning before building on it.

slides.name: 25 · The weak answer: what is wrong

params.text: The weak answer: what is wrong
A hard drive and RAM are not parts of the CPU.

They are storage and memory, outside the CPU.
It needs the CPU’s own parts, each with its job.
Ask the writer: “Take one component. What does it do while a program runs?”

slides.notes: 1 min.

slides.name: 26 · The stable answer: which lines are right?

params.text: The stable answer: which lines are right?

params.data:
Part	The stable answer says
Control unit	decodes instructions and sends control signals.
ALU	the brain of the CPU.
Registers	store data.
Cache	stores data.
Clock	controls the speed of the computer.

slides.notes: 1.5 min. Students read each line and decide: exact job, or not? Then vote.

feedback.prompt: How many lines give the exact job?

slides.name: 27 · The stable answer: marked

params.data:
Part	Verdict	Why
Control unit	✓ Exact job	It names the two things the control unit does: it decodes instructions and sends control signals.
ALU	✗ A label, not a job	“The brain” does not say what it does: arithmetic and logic.
Registers	✗ Too vague	“Store data” could be any memory. Say what they hold and where.
Cache	✗ Too vague	“Stores data” again. Say what it keeps, and why: so the CPU does not wait.
Clock	✗ Wrong job	It sends timing signals. It does not “control the speed”.

slides.notes:
1 min. One line is right: the control unit.
Only the control unit has its exact purpose. “Stores data” could be any memory, so it says nothing about registers or cache; the ALU as “the brain” is a label; and the clock sends timing signals, it does not “control the speed”.

slides.name: 28 · Fix the stable answer

params.text:
Task (2 min): rewrite the four wrong lines in your book. Give each part its exact job, with no labels.
ALU: …
Registers: …
Cache: …
Clock: …

slides.notes: 2 min. The fix is precision, not reasoning: adding “because” would not fix “the brain of the CPU”.

slides.name: 29 · The excellent answer

params.data:
Part	The excellent answer says
Control unit	decodes instructions and sends control signals that coordinate the other parts
ALU	performs arithmetic and logical operations
Registers	tiny, fast stores inside the CPU
PC	the PC holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched
Cache	fast memory close to the processor, for frequently used data and instructions
Clock	provides timing signals that keep the CPU's operations in step

slides.notes: 1 min. Compare it with your fixed lines, one by one.

slides.name: 41 · For the teacher: what each answer shows

params.text: For the teacher: what each answer shows

params.data:
Answer	Structure	Process to investigate	Probe
Weak	Prestructural	Retrieval	“Take one component. What does it do while a program runs?”
Stable	Unistructural	Comprehension	“What exactly does it hold or do? Say it without a label.”
Excellent	Multistructural	None shown on this task	A fresh, independent task

slides.notes:
Teacher-facing: hidden in the student copy. Readings of answers, not of minds: each is a possibility to test with its probe.
Weak: Possible explanation: Names storage and memory, not the CPU’s own components. Probe: “Take one component. What does it do while a program runs?” If that is not enough: “The PC holds an address. The address of what?” Then withdraw the hint and ask for the full description of each component. Teaching response, if the probe confirms it: secure the term and its exact meaning before building on it.
Stable: Possible explanation: Only the control unit has its exact purpose. “Stores data” could be any memory, so it says nothing about registers or cache; the ALU as “the brain” is a label; and the clock sends timing signals, it does not “control the speed”. Probe: “What exactly does it hold or do? Say it without a label.” Teaching response, if the probe confirms it: secure the term and its exact meaning before building on it.
Excellent: On this task, nothing shown missing. Next check, not an observation: A fresh, independent task: “Describe the main parts of a computer around the CPU: main memory, secondary storage, input and output.” Teaching response: if it does not transfer, check the new topic's knowledge first, then return to the hint.
